English | [中文](README.zh.md)
DS Bot is an open-source project built on [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH), available as a standalone desktop app or as a DSH plugin. It turns DSH into bots that you create, talk to and work with.

## Install
**Desktop app (Windows, macOS, Linux)**
The desktop app brings its own DSH, so you don't need to install DSH first. Download the installer for your system from [Releases](https://github.com/Fei2411/DS-Bot/releases/latest), open it, and set up a model in Settings (it can also copy your existing bot team from DSH).
If your system warns about an unsigned app: on Windows select **More info** → **Run anyway**; on macOS open **System Settings** → **Privacy & Security** and select **Open Anyway**.
**As a plugin in DSH**
First install DSH and set up at least one model in it. DS Bot uses the models from DSH.
- **DSH Desktop**: In the sidebar, select **Plugins** → **Add plugin**, enter `ds-bot` (in mainland China, set **Registry** to **Mainland China mirror**), then select **Install** and **Enable now**.
- **DSH Web** (needs Node.js `22.19` or later, and pnpm):
```sh
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.2-rc.1 plugin --profile web add ds-bot
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.2-rc.1 web
```
**Docker (NAS, Linux server)**
See [`docker/README.md`](docker/README.md).
## Setup
I strongly recommend that you set up your other bots and group chats by just talking to a bot.

DS Bot selects its `auto` search provider for the whole profile. If you disable `web-search-auto`, also select another registered search provider in that profile. # Pi Bot
**An open-source, local-first AI agent team for your desktop.** Named AI Bots work on your own
computer: chat with one or put several in a group chat, and they plan, run commands, edit files,
browse the web and use your computer, while every risky step waits for your approval. Runs on
macOS, Windows and Linux, with an Android app. Built on the [pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi)
agent kernel.
 ▶  Watch the 60-second video  ·  Download  ·  User guide  ·  Online docs  
[English](README.md) · [中文](README.zh-CN.md) · [日本語](README.ja.md)
Pi Bot is a desktop app in which a team of named Bots works on your own computer. You chat with a
Bot directly or put several in a group chat, give them a working folder, and they plan, run
commands, edit files and hand work to each other, while every risky step waits for your approval.
The "brain" runs on your machine too: chats, files, memory and keys stay local, and only the
model provider you choose sees the prompts you send.
Website and downloads:   · User guide: [docs/guide](docs/guide/README.md) · Online docs:  
## What it does
- **Bots and roles.** Create Bots with a name, a role (developer, researcher, writer, translator,
  …), their own model, skills, permissions and memory.
- **Direct and group chats.** A group has a coordinator that plans, hands steps to members and
  collects the results; you confirm the plan before it runs.
- **Working folders and changes.** Bots work inside folders you choose. Every change is listed,
  reviewable and, on macOS, restorable from automatic checkpoints.
- **Approvals and permissions.** Every tool call goes through one policy engine. Commands run in
  a sandbox ([`@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime`](https://github.com/anthropics/sandbox-runtime)),
  and approvals, commands and anything sent outward are written to an audit log.
- **Routines and to-dos.** Scheduled, folder-triggered and connection-triggered tasks.
- **Connections.** Apps, MCP servers, skills and knowledge bases.
- **Models.** Local models through Ollama, OpenRouter, your own API keys, and supported
  subscription sign-ins.
- **More devices, optional.** An Android app, runners on other computers or servers, a relay you
  can host yourself, and use from editors over ACP.
Pi Bot runs on macOS 13 Ventura or later, Windows 10 / 11 and 64-bit Linux. It has no telemetry,
and Pi Bot's own servers never receive your chats or files. Besides the model provider you choose,

top10.descricao_en: Long-term memory runtime for AI agents — plain Markdown as the source of truth, local ranked retrieval, and an independent sleep-time Manage layer. Claude Code and Codex share one store. No API key.
top10.readme:
### agent-memory: the long-term memory runtime for AI agents
 Invariants  ·  Skill  ·  Issues 
***
An agent that closes its session forgets everything it learned in it. agent-memory is the
runtime that fixes that, for any agent — not only coding ones. Markdown files in one store are
the single source of truth, the SQLite index beside them is a cache you can delete at any time,
and Claude Code, Codex CLI, Muse Code, and anything else that can run a shell command share
that store.
Retrieval is local and ranked, and it answers with paths rather than pasted text — the agent
opens each hit only as deep as the task needs. Writes do not wait for the agent to remember to
make them: they fire at conversation boundaries. A sleep-time pass then consolidates and
forgets by value, on its own clock. None of it needs an API key.
## Two lines, one store
Agent memory has grown along two architectural lines. One builds a **retrieval engine** —
embeddings, a knowledge graph, a ranking pipeline — which finds the right thing, but hands the
agent an opaque chunk it cannot inspect and a store it cannot migrate off. The other hands the
agent a **filesystem** — markdown it reads directly, browsable with `ls` and `grep` — which is
legible and costs nothing to run, but does not rank, and stops scaling the moment the tree
outgrows a listing.
agent-memory is the two of them in one store: the retrieval engine indexes a filesystem the
agent can also just read. Relations live as links inside the memories, a local index ranks
them, and every hit resolves to a whole markdown file on disk. Recall gains the precision of a
graph and a vector search without giving up a plain directory an agent can walk — and it stays
fast, because nothing in the read path calls a model or crosses a network.
## Retrieve by path, then read by level
Recall does not paste text into your context. It answers with an L0 list — one-line abstract,
file path, anchor, score — and the agent opens what it wants at the depth the task needs:
```bash
mem recall "why files instead of a database"    # L0 list, 8 entries by default
mem recall "why files instead of a database" --limit 20  # more Memory candidates
mem read   --level outline                 # headings only; or abstract, or full
mem context "why files instead of a database"   # both in one call, top few expanded in full
mem trace                                   # cited raw messages, when needed
```
Index line → abstract → full file → raw material: each rung costs

**LoopForge** is a self-hosted workspace where your team ships software with coding agents. Describe what you need to **Main Bot** in chat: it opens a Docker sandbox, checks out your repositories, delegates to project roles, and opens the PR. When a way of working proves itself, save it as an **SOP** (a standard workflow of agents, scripts and human gates) so the next requirement is delivered the same way, with review and approval built in.
Coding-agent CLIs do the work: CodeBuddy, Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor CLI, Antigravity, Kimi Code, Pi, DeepSeek Harness and ZCode. LoopForge adds the roles, sandboxes, checkpoints and history around them, all on your own infrastructure under the MIT license.
## Two ways to work
| | **Chat with Main Bot** | **Run an SOP** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Best for | Exploring, quick fixes, iterating with the agent | Repeatable delivery with fixed stages and sign-off |
| How it runs | Main Bot opens a [conversation workspace](docs/conversation-workspaces.md) (a Docker sandbox with your repos) on demand and calls project roles as subagents | The engine runs Agent, Script, Human-gate and sub-SOP nodes in order, in their own sandbox |
| You stay in control by | Queuing or steering messages mid-reply, and pausing, resuming or taking over a running SOP from chat | Approving at human gates, sending work back to a chosen step, retrying or rerunning from any node |
| Delivers | A PR/MR, or a direct merge into a shared branch (`mode=direct`) | Documents, code or a PR, plus per-node artifacts and logs |
Both paths track the same **requirements**, so every change, whether made in chat or by an SOP, links back to what was asked for and counts toward delivery and cost reports.
  The chat home. Type a request,  @  a role, skill, requirement, SOP or repository, and pick the executor, model and permission mode per conversation.  
## Why LoopForge
Ask a coding agent to "fix this bug" and the result depends on that run. It might skip the plan, forget the tests, review its own code, or stop halfway without anyone noticing. That's fine for a demo, but it isn't how a team ships.
- **Repeatable.** Same SOP, same stages, same checks for every requirement. Start from built-in backend, frontend, bug

top10.descricao_en: Desktop app that records your on-screen work session and uses the GitHub Copilot SDK to reconstruct it as an intent + ordered steps, then builds a reusable Skill or Automation for Microsoft Autopilots like Scout, Microsoft Copilot Cowork, or Copilot Studio.
top10.readme:
# Skill Recorder
**Record yourself doing a task once, then turn it into a skill your AI agent can repeat.**
> [!TIP]
> **Want to install Skill Recorder? [Go to the latest release](https://github.com/microsoft/skill-recorder/releases/latest).**
> Scroll to **Commit-pinned installation** and copy the complete command for your
> operating system. It is ready to paste: you do not need to edit it or download
> the source code yourself. [Step-by-step instructions below](#install-it).
Skill Recorder captures a real work session on your screen: the clicks, the app and
window switches, the pages you visit, commands/output from its optional recorded terminal,
and (if you want) your spoken narration. It then uses
the **GitHub Copilot CLI** to reconstruct *what you actually did* as a clear **intent plus
an ordered list of steps**. From there, one step turns that single run into something an
agent can reuse:
- a **Skill**: a `SKILL.md` procedure an agent runs on demand, or
- an **Automation**: the same procedure on a schedule or trigger.
Both prefer the agent's **native tools** (like the `gh` CLI or `web_fetch`) over replaying
UI clicks, and generalize from your one example, so recording yourself submitting *one*
form can teach the agent to submit *all* of them.
    
## How it works
1. 🔴 **Record.** Hit record (or `⌘⇧R` / `Ctrl+Shift+R` from anywhere) and just do your
   task. Skill Recorder captures your screen and activity locally, in the background.
2. 🎛️ **Control.** While recording, a small always-on-top bar shows capture,
   microphone, and recorded-terminal state. Open the session-scoped terminal, mute,
   unmute, or switch mics, then finish or discard with confirmation.
3. 🧠 **Analyze.** Click Analyze and your selected AI provider reconstructs one overall intent and
   an ordered list of steps. Review and edit until it reads right.
4. ✨ **Create.** From an approved analysis, generate a reusable **Skill** and/or a
   scheduled **Automation**.
For skills, **Review SKILL.md** optionally shows the complete, read-only file text
(including frontmatter) before installation or export. Preparing a preview writes
no skill files. Close and reopen it without regenerating; Add/Export from either
surface uses that exact preview. Editing the plan discards the preview. You can
still choose Add/Export directly without reviewing or adding a confirmation step.
Review provides visibility into the generated instructions, not a security guarantee.
